all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] isRemoteDefault assumes a remote name is a single path segment, but git accepts remote names that contain '/'. I checked this in a temp repo: `git remote add team/up <url>` succeeds. So refs/remotes/team/up/main splits into remote "team" and branch "up/main", is not treated as a remote default, and is never passed to the range leg's `--not`. For users whose upstream remote name contains a slash, the stale-local-main problem fixed in d994410 comes back: a branch cut from a fresh team/up/main while local main lags pulls merged branches' runs into its range. This over-blocks and never fails open. A precise fix would read the remote names (`git remote`, or the prefixes from for-each-ref) and match refs/remotes/<known-remote>/main|master.

[ADVISORY] fsm init treats any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` check the same as git's "no" (exit 1): a timeout, a spawn failure or exit 128 just skips the fold. scope.Load does the opposite and leaves the scope unknown when this same check fails with anything other than exit 1 (scope.go `case code(err) != 1: return s`). Everywhere else in init (symbolic-ref, for-each-ref) a git failure goes through gitFailed/ERR_GIT, but this call does not. On a case-insensitive filesystem with HEAD spelled `Feat` for branch `feat`, a transient git failure at this call makes init record branch `Feat` without any error. Status later folds Current to `feat`, so the run matches only while its head is in range. After a rebase it is classed as orphaned (no branch `Feat` is listed) and stops blocking. This needs a transient git failure during init together with a mis-cased checkout, so it is not normal usage. The fix is to route `err != nil || code > 1` through gitFailed("rev-parse", ...).

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new fold check ignores a failed `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<spelling>`. Any failure (a timeout, or an exit code other than 1) leaves the mis-spelled HEAD unfolded, and init records it (e.g. "Feat") without error. scope.Load does the same check but fails closed: an exit code other than 1 leaves the scope unknown. So the two consumers of the one rule handle a failed check differently, and init differs from its own gitFailed handling of symbolic-ref and for-each-ref failures. This needs a case-insensitive filesystem, a mis-cased checkout and a transient git failure during init. The run is then recorded under "Feat", while status on the same checkout folds Current to "feat". The name leg no longer matches, and "Feat" is not a listed branch. Once the branch is rebased and the head leaves the range, the run is classified orphaned and silently stops blocking. The fix is to return gitFailed("rev-parse", code, err) when err != nil or code is neither 0 nor 1.

[ADVISORY] isRemoteDefault treats the first path segment after refs/remotes/ as the remote name. Git allows remote names that contain a slash (`git remote add team/upstream <url>` yields refs/remotes/team/upstream/main). That remote's default branch is therefore never excluded from the range leg. To tell origin/alice/main apart from a slash-named remote's main, the check needs the configured remote names (`git remote`, or remote.*.fetch). This needs a slash-named remote as the only up-to-date copy of main and a stale local main. The stale-main over-block fixed in d994410 then comes back: runs of branches already merged upstream fall into the range of a branch cut from that remote's main, and they block a branch that cannot act on them. The failure blocks too much and never clears a gate.

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new case-fold check handles a failing `rev-parse --verify` differently from scope.Load. Load treats any exit other than 1 as a git failure and leaves the scope unknown (fail closed). init silently skips the fold on any failure (a spawn error, a timeout, exit 128) and records HEAD's mis-spelled name (e.g. "Feat") without raising ERR_GIT. Every other git call in this block goes through gitFailed. This needs a transient git failure during init on a case-insensitive checkout where HEAD is spelled differently from the listed branch. Then the run is recorded under a name git never lists. It keeps blocking only through the range leg. After the branch is rebased, status classifies it as orphaned, so the abandoned run stops blocking. The window is narrow, but the handling is inconsistent with the fail-closed rule stated for the branch scope. Treating code != 0 && code != 1 (or err != nil) as gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) would match Load.

[ADVISORY] Case folding now only happens when `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<HEAD spelling>` resolves, and that is not a stable sign of a case-insensitive filesystem. The mis-spelled HEAD resolves only while the branch is a loose ref. Once `git gc` or auto-gc runs `pack-refs --all`, the packed-refs lookup is case-sensitive. I checked this on macOS: `checkout -b feat; checkout main; checkout Feat` gives HEAD refs/heads/Feat and rev-parse rc=0. After `git pack-refs --all`, rev-parse gives rc=1. At that point Load keeps Current="Feat", which is not folded, and ForkPoint on the now-unborn HEAD returns no error, so the scope is known with an empty range. Runs that init recorded as "feat" (folded earlier, while the ref was loose) then classify as other-branch. Before ce80bb4 the fold was unconditional and those runs kept blocking. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a branch checked out with the wrong case stops being blocked by its own abandoned runs after the next auto-gc packs refs. Git itself shows the checkout as unborn in that state ("No commits yet"), so the breakage is visible and needs an earlier mis-cased checkout. That is why this is advisory. A more stable signal would be `core.ignorecase`, which git sets at init on case-insensitive filesystems, used instead of or alongside the resolve check.

[ADVISORY] fsm init ignores any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` check: a timeout, a spawn error or an exit code other than 1 just skips the fold, and init records the HEAD spelling (for example "Feat"). scope.Load treats the same failure as unknown, which fails closed. Later, when status folds the spelling to "feat", it no longer matches the recorded "Feat". If git fails transiently during init on a mis-cased checkout, the run is recorded under a spelling no branch has. After a rebase moves its head out of range, the run classifies as orphaned and stops blocking. This needs both a mis-cased HEAD and a transient git failure, so the chance is low. A fix would call gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) when the code is not 1, matching the symbolic-ref and for-each-ref handling above it.

[ADVISORY] The only test that exercises init's new fold path (rev-parse --verify of the mis-spelled HEAD, then Canonical) and the new canonical --for-branch comparison (`scope.Canonical(branch, branches) != current`, which records `current` on a restatement) skips itself on any case-sensitive filesystem. CI runs on ubuntu-latest, and in a golang:1.26 Linux container it reports SKIP. So CI never runs the run.go lines 302-316 changed in ce80bb4. scope.Load has a fake-git unit test for the same decision (TestLoadFoldsOnlyAResolvingSpelling), but init has none that doesn't depend on the filesystem. A regression in init's fold or --for-branch restatement logic (for example comparing the raw branch again, or recording the HEAD spelling) would pass CI and only show up on a macOS developer machine. A mis-cased run name reads as orphaned once its head leaves the range, and then blocks nothing.

[ADVISORY] init treats every rev-parse outcome except success (err == nil && code == 0) as 'the spelling does not resolve'. That includes a timeout or spawn error (err != nil) and a real git failure (code 128). scope.Load makes the same check fail closed: code != 1 leaves the scope unknown. The two paths now disagree, and no test covers init's failure case (Load's 128 case is tested). On a case-insensitive filesystem, a transient git failure at this call makes init record the HEAD spelling (e.g. "Feat") instead of the listed branch "feat". status never matches that run by name, so after a rebase it is orphaned and stops blocking. Unlikely, but it's the only fail-open spot in this commit. Returning gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) when code is neither 0 nor 1 would match Load.

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new case-fold check treats any failure of `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<HEAD spelling>` as 'does not resolve'. That covers a timeout, a spawn failure or exit 128, not only git's exit 1. Every other git call in init returns ERR_GIT through gitFailed, and scope.Load fails closed on the same call (`code(err) != 1` leaves the scope unknown). Here init quietly records the mis-cased spelling (e.g. `Feat` instead of `feat`). This only happens on a case-insensitive filesystem when the checkout was done with a mis-cased name and rev-parse fails transiently. The run would then be recorded under a branch name git does not list. After the branch is rebased, the name leg never matches and the run is orphaned, so it stops blocking. It is very unlikely in normal use, but it is inconsistent with the fail-closed contract. A fix: return gitFailed when err != nil or code is anything other than 0 or 1.

[ADVISORY] fsm init treats any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` probe the same as git's plain "no" (exit 1). A spawn failure, a timeout or an exit 128 all skip the fold without saying so, and the run is recorded under HEAD's mis-cased spelling. scope.Load does this differently (scope.go:154-159): a non-1 exit leaves the scope unknown, so it fails closed. Every other git call in init goes through gitFailed and returns ERR_GIT. This needs a case-insensitive filesystem, a mis-cased checkout (`git checkout Feat` onto feat) and a transient git failure at exactly this call during init. When all three happen, the run is recorded as "Feat" while status later folds Current to "feat". After a rebase the recorded head is out of range, so the run is classed Orphaned and no longer blocks the branch it reviewed. The chance is low, since the git calls just before it succeeded. Handling code != 1 (and err != nil) via gitFailed("rev-parse", code, err) would match Load's fail-closed rule.

So refs/remotes/team/up/main splits into remote "team" and branch "up/main", is not treated as a remote default, and is never passed to the range leg's `--not`. For users whose upstream remote name contains a slash, the stale-local-main problem fixed in d994410 comes back: a branch cut from a fresh team/up/main while local main lags pulls merged branches' runs into its range. This over-blocks and never fails open. A precise fix would read the remote names (`git remote`, or the prefixes from for-each-ref) and match refs/remotes/<known-remote>/main|master.

[ADVISORY] fsm init treats any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` check the same as git's "no" (exit 1): a timeout, a spawn failure or exit 128 just skips the fold. scope.Load does the opposite and leaves the scope unknown when this same check fails with anything other than exit 1 (scope.go `case code(err) != 1: return s`). Everywhere else in init (symbolic-ref, for-each-ref) a git failure goes through gitFailed/ERR_GIT, but this call does not. On a case-insensitive filesystem with HEAD spelled `Feat` for branch `feat`, a transient git failure at this call makes init record branch `Feat` without any error. Status later folds Current to `feat`, so the run matches only while its head is in range. After a rebase it is classed as orphaned (no branch `Feat` is listed) and stops blocking. This needs a transient git failure during init together with a mis-cased checkout, so it is not normal usage. The fix is to route `err != nil || code > 1` through gitFailed("rev-parse", ...).

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new fold check ignores a failed `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<spelling>`. Any failure (a timeout, or an exit code other than 1) leaves the mis-spelled HEAD unfolded, and init records it (e.g. "Feat") without error. scope.Load does the same check but fails closed: an exit code other than 1 leaves the scope unknown. So the two consumers of the one rule handle a failed check differently, and init differs from its own gitFailed handling of symbolic-ref and for-each-ref failures. This needs a case-insensitive filesystem, a mis-cased checkout and a transient git failure during init. The run is then recorded under "Feat", while status on the same checkout folds Current to "feat". The name leg no longer matches, and "Feat" is not a listed branch. Once the branch is rebased and the head leaves the range, the run is classified orphaned and silently stops blocking. The fix is to return gitFailed("rev-parse", code, err) when err != nil or code is neither 0 nor 1.

[ADVISORY] isRemoteDefault treats the first path segment after refs/remotes/ as the remote name. Git allows remote names that contain a slash (`git remote add team/upstream <url>` yields refs/remotes/team/upstream/main). That remote's default branch is therefore never excluded from the range leg. To tell origin/alice/main apart from a slash-named remote's main, the check needs the configured remote names (`git remote`, or remote.*.fetch). This needs a slash-named remote as the only up-to-date copy of main and a stale local main. The stale-main over-block fixed in d994410 then comes back: runs of branches already merged upstream fall into the range of a branch cut from that remote's main, and they block a branch that cannot act on them. The failure blocks too much and never clears a gate.

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new case-fold check handles a failing `rev-parse --verify` differently from scope.Load. Load treats any exit other than 1 as a git failure and leaves the scope unknown (fail closed). init silently skips the fold on any failure (a spawn error, a timeout, exit 128) and records HEAD's mis-spelled name (e.g. "Feat") without raising ERR_GIT. Every other git call in this block goes through gitFailed. This needs a transient git failure during init on a case-insensitive checkout where HEAD is spelled differently from the listed branch. Then the run is recorded under a name git never lists. It keeps blocking only through the range leg. After the branch is rebased, status classifies it as orphaned, so the abandoned run stops blocking. The window is narrow, but the handling is inconsistent with the fail-closed rule stated for the branch scope. Treating code != 0 && code != 1 (or err != nil) as gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) would match Load.

[ADVISORY] Case folding now only happens when `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<HEAD spelling>` resolves, and that is not a stable sign of a case-insensitive filesystem. The mis-spelled HEAD resolves only while the branch is a loose ref. Once `git gc` or auto-gc runs `pack-refs --all`, the packed-refs lookup is case-sensitive. I checked this on macOS: `checkout -b feat; checkout main; checkout Feat` gives HEAD refs/heads/Feat and rev-parse rc=0. After `git pack-refs --all`, rev-parse gives rc=1. At that point Load keeps Current="Feat", which is not folded, and ForkPoint on the now-unborn HEAD returns no error, so the scope is known with an empty range. Runs that init recorded as "feat" (folded earlier, while the ref was loose) then classify as other-branch. Before ce80bb4 the fold was unconditional and those runs kept blocking. On a case-insensitive filesystem, a branch checked out with the wrong case stops being blocked by its own abandoned runs after the next auto-gc packs refs. Git itself shows the checkout as unborn in that state ("No commits yet"), so the breakage is visible and needs an earlier mis-cased checkout. That is why this is advisory. A more stable signal would be `core.ignorecase`, which git sets at init on case-insensitive filesystems, used instead of or alongside the resolve check.

[ADVISORY] fsm init ignores any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` check: a timeout, a spawn error or an exit code other than 1 just skips the fold, and init records the HEAD spelling (for example "Feat"). scope.Load treats the same failure as unknown, which fails closed. Later, when status folds the spelling to "feat", it no longer matches the recorded "Feat". If git fails transiently during init on a mis-cased checkout, the run is recorded under a spelling no branch has. After a rebase moves its head out of range, the run classifies as orphaned and stops blocking. This needs both a mis-cased HEAD and a transient git failure, so the chance is low. A fix would call gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) when the code is not 1, matching the symbolic-ref and for-each-ref handling above it.

[ADVISORY] The only test that exercises init's new fold path (rev-parse --verify of the mis-spelled HEAD, then Canonical) and the new canonical --for-branch comparison (`scope.Canonical(branch, branches) != current`, which records `current` on a restatement) skips itself on any case-sensitive filesystem. CI runs on ubuntu-latest, and in a golang:1.26 Linux container it reports SKIP. So CI never runs the run.go lines 302-316 changed in ce80bb4. scope.Load has a fake-git unit test for the same decision (TestLoadFoldsOnlyAResolvingSpelling), but init has none that doesn't depend on the filesystem. A regression in init's fold or --for-branch restatement logic (for example comparing the raw branch again, or recording the HEAD spelling) would pass CI and only show up on a macOS developer machine. A mis-cased run name reads as orphaned once its head leaves the range, and then blocks nothing.

[ADVISORY] init treats every rev-parse outcome except success (err == nil && code == 0) as 'the spelling does not resolve'. That includes a timeout or spawn error (err != nil) and a real git failure (code 128). scope.Load makes the same check fail closed: code != 1 leaves the scope unknown. The two paths now disagree, and no test covers init's failure case (Load's 128 case is tested). On a case-insensitive filesystem, a transient git failure at this call makes init record the HEAD spelling (e.g. "Feat") instead of the listed branch "feat". status never matches that run by name, so after a rebase it is orphaned and stops blocking. Unlikely, but it's the only fail-open spot in this commit. Returning gitFailed("rev-parse", ...) when code is neither 0 nor 1 would match Load.

[ADVISORY] fsm init's new case-fold check treats any failure of `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<HEAD spelling>` as 'does not resolve'. That covers a timeout, a spawn failure or exit 128, not only git's exit 1. Every other git call in init returns ERR_GIT through gitFailed, and scope.Load fails closed on the same call (`code(err) != 1` leaves the scope unknown). Here init quietly records the mis-cased spelling (e.g. `Feat` instead of `feat`). This only happens on a case-insensitive filesystem when the checkout was done with a mis-cased name and rev-parse fails transiently. The run would then be recorded under a branch name git does not list. After the branch is rebased, the name leg never matches and the run is orphaned, so it stops blocking. It is very unlikely in normal use, but it is inconsistent with the fail-closed contract. A fix: return gitFailed when err != nil or code is anything other than 0 or 1.

[ADVISORY] fsm init treats any failure of the new `rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<current>` probe the same as git's plain "no" (exit 1).
